newsitem.title: USA: GFOA urges SEC to relax customer account form plan.
newsitem.headline: GFOA urges SEC to relax customer account form plan.

text.p: State and local finance officers said they support an SEC proposal that dealers keep account forms for every customer, but added that requiring them to annually update the documents may be "burdensome."

The Government Finance Officers Association offered its remarks in a four-page comment letter to the Securities and Exchange Commission. The letter offers a two-part solution to the account form-update problem.
The SEC's proposed amendment to its books and records rules would require broker-dealers to maintain account forms for each customer.
The forms would discuss a customer's background and his or her investment objectives and constraints.
GFOA said most broker-dealers already collect the information about their customers, so the proposal should not be troublesome. But the group added that annual updates may be a problem for firms.
"We suggest the following alternatives," GFOA said.
The rules could give institutional investors the option of waiving their annual updates from dealers, GFOA said.

But before a waiver could occur, dealers would have to enter into a "comprehensive investment agreement" with each buyer that requires each buyer to have an "investment policy" and provide it to the dealer.

In the case of retail investors, SEC should require dealers to send customers annual notices reminding them that their account forms may need to be updated if their circumstances have changed, GFOA said.
The notices should ask retail buyers to verify their addresses, telephone numbers and other key information.
